intro: You have arrived at Antiochia ad Pisidiam, Antioch of Pisidia, an ancient city in Isparta province whose story runs from the 3rd century BC to the 6th century AD. This was a Roman colony where Paul the Apostle preached, and its proudest monument is the Temple of Augustus, the Augusteum. Let us walk through it together.
history: The city was born as a frontier post. Around 275 BC the Seleucid dynasty founded it to control Galatian raids. Then, in 25 BC, Augustus made it a Roman colony called 'Colonia Caesarea'. Soon a new voice was heard here: Paul the Apostle preached with Barnabas in the local synagogue. That visit was never forgotten, and the city remained an important Christian pilgrimage centre into the Byzantine period.
structure-1: You are now standing before the Temple of Augustus, the Augusteum. This temple was dedicated to the cult of Augustus himself. Pause for a moment and imagine the worshippers who once climbed towards it.
structure-3: Next comes the Propylon, the Monumental Gate. This was the grand entrance that framed the sanctuary at Antiochia. Picture yourself passing beneath it, with the sacred precinct opening up beyond.
structure-4: Here stands the Church of St. Paul, also known as the Great Basilica. This great basilica at Antiochia is associated with St Paul, whose preaching gave the city its lasting place in Christian memory.
structure-5: Now look for the Aqueducts and the Nymphaeum. The aqueducts brought water to the city, and the monumental fountain put it proudly on display. Can you imagine the sound of running water in the heart of this Roman town?
highlights: As you wander on, don't miss the Theatre, another corner of this Roman city waiting to be discovered.
facts: Did you know? In Roman times the city's main street, the 'Cardo Maximus', led straight up to the Temple of Augustus to promote the imperial cult, and the community here was known as the 'People of Augustus'. It was here that Saint Paul preached his first major sermon; this is the city whose synagogue Acts names. One of the most important Latin copies of Augustus' Res Gestae, his own account of his deeds, was also found here. And one more detail: the city was founded as a colony settled with retired legionaries, which is why its street plan follows the logic of a military camp.
outro: This brings our tour of Antiochia ad Pisidiam, Antioch of Pisidia to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
